lines.trans: Viktor Petrovich, this guy will not work here!
Just a second, since when do you give orders here?
I am the restaurant art director and know our standards!
Senya, say loudly, who is the boss in this kitchen?
All the cooks know perfectly well that I am the boss here.
You are hiring the first random person from the street!
I alone decide who works in my kitchen!
You will regret this strange and foolish decision.
Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!
You will work on a two-on, two-off schedule.
This is simply outrageous and completely unacceptable behavior!
And you can go command your waiters.
Create a wonderful atmosphere in the hall of our establishment!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'art director', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: I am the art director of the restaurant.
Vika works as the restaurant art director.
This is Viktoria Sergeyevna, our art director.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'atmosphere, vibe' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Создавайте прекрасную атмосферу в зале нашего заведения!
examples.trans: Create a wonderful atmosphere in the hall of our establishment!

examples.text: Там великолепный вид и совершенно волшебная атмосфера.
examples.trans: There is a magnificent view and completely magical atmosphere.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'змутительный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('outrageous, scandalous').

examples.text: Это просто возмутительное и совершенно недопустимое поведение!
examples.trans: This is simply outrageous and completely unacceptable behavior!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('oncoming, random').

examples.text: Вы нанимаете первого встречного человека с улицы!
examples.trans: You are hiring the first random person from the street!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'schedule'.

examples.text: У Самсонова в графике стоит важная встреча?
examples.trans: Is there an important meeting on Samsonov's schedule?

examples.text: Будешь работать по графику два через два.
examples.trans: You will work on a two-on, two-off schedule.

meanings.note: поставить громко = to put a phone on speaker

examples.text: Не говорите так громко, дети спят.
examples.trans: Don't speak so loudly, the children are asleep.

examples.text: Ой, это Илона! Я громко поставлю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's Ilona! I'll put it on speaker.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ведение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'establishment, institution' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.

examples.text: Это очень популярное заведение в городе.
examples.trans: This is a very popular establishment in town.

examples.text: Как ты посмел прийти в моё заведение?
examples.trans: How did you dare to come into my establishment?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hall', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('living room') (regional/colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: to command, be in charge, give orders
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to command, to give orders', paired with 'скомандовать'.

examples.text: Да я на всё готов! Командуйте.
examples.trans: Why, I'm ready for anything! Give the orders.

examples.text: Здесь командую только я и никто больше.
examples.trans: Only I command here and no one else.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне вы главный, так что смело командуйте!
examples.trans: Today you are in charge in the kitchen, so give the orders boldly!

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hire, employ', paired with 'нанять'.

examples.text: Вы нанимаете первого встречного человека с улицы!
examples.trans: You are hiring the first random person from the street!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'допустимый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('unacceptable, inadmissible').

examples.text: Это просто возмутительное и совершенно недопустимое поведение!
examples.trans: This is simply outrageous and completely unacceptable behavior!

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'excellently'.
Secondary conversational sense ('great!, excellent!') (as a one-word reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, это не обман. В этот раз всё будет официально.
examples.trans: No, it's not a trick. This time everything will be official.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('guy, lad, young man') (informal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'first', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ведение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'behaviour, conduct' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She was fired for her conduct.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: ты ещё пожалеешь! = you'll be sorry!
Secondary conversational sense ('to feel sorry for') (+ accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, сколько у меня денег? Ты ещё пожалеешь!
examples.trans: Do you know how much money I have? You'll be sorry!

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

examples.text: Посмотри, какой у нас город прекрасный. Озёра, луга.
examples.trans: Look what a beautiful town we have. Lakes, meadows.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to accept, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to decide', forming an aspectual pair with 'решить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'decision' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('solution') (to a problem) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I am forced to cancel my decision.
We have already made a decision.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: affectionate diminutive of секунда; секундочку! = just a second!

examples.trans: Wait, just now, one little second.
Just a second, I'll be right back!
Yes, of course. Wait, just now, one little second.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'completely'.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оздавать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to create', forming an aspectual pair with 'создать'.

examples.trans: You create unnecessary problems for us.
The artist creates a new painting.

examples.text: Ты всегда создаёшь нам большие проблемы.
examples.trans: You always create big problems for us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тандарт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'standard' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я арт-директор ресторана и знаю наши стандарты!
examples.trans: I am the restaurant art director and know our standards!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: на улице = out on the street / outside
на улице холодно = it's cold outside

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
There are reporters out on the street!

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'staff, personnel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
